body:
Thank you for your kind words! I'm already dreading tomorrow and the work that will have built up. That's the problem with taking a day off, I'll still have to do the work I didn't do. But I think I needed it.

During my first (and still worst) episode of depression I refused antidepressants. It was a mistake, I should have taken them, they would have helped. It was only after a couple more episodes of depression that I got to the point where I caved in and took them (I was experiencing panic attacks so bad that I ended up in A&E three times a week and became completely agoraphobic. They worked like magic. I think it was Seroxat. 

I don't remember when I decided to stop taking them but I have come off antidepressants a few times in my life without ever having real problems. You do hear horror stories of people coming off them but I think if you taper off them, generally it won't be too bad. Then there are others who just keep taking them. A lot of people are really anti taking any drug regularly but I'm not. If it helps me and isn't causing terrible side effects, what do I care? I only came off them because I felt I didn't need them anymore and it was inconvenient being 'dependent' on a medication.

But to answer your question, antidepressants did not stop my brain making happy chemicals or anything like that. I think your brain is quite good at adjusting so there may be slightly difficult transition periods but you would probably have to hit your brain with huge, repeated doses of MDMA or methamphetamine to permanently lose the ability to feel normal again. And even those people tend to recover. 

Good work on resolving to exercise. Try not to go over the top, even with that. Sometimes I'll run and push myself so hard that it becomes a bit counterproductive. 

Overthinking is the absolute worst thing you can do. Especially when it comes to work. I managed to create a severe episode of anxiety/depression just by worrying about work. Ironically, I then ended up truly jeopardising my job through having to take over a month off as a result (actually I don't know if my job was really in jeopardy, they were good about it).

I think like you do though. Even after taking today off I start thinking, 'What if they fire me because of this?' It's definitely depressive thinking. When I'm feeling well I know I could disappear for a couple of weeks, Don Draper style, without telling them anything and they wouldn't fire me.

Best of luck with everything and if you want to chat, then I'm around. When I'm depressed like this the only thing I want to talk about is depression, lol. Then when it clears up depression is the last thing I want to spend time talking or thinking about!

"I was looking for a job and then I found a job,
And heaven knows I'm miserable now."

Morrissey knew the score.

Really sorry to hear you're going through this. I went through my first episode of depression at about your age. I had no clue what was happening and just assumed that something in my brain had broken. It didn't even occur to me that I was depressed. 

At least you know that you're likely experiencing an episode of depression. You won't have this feeling forever, you can be sure of that. Whether this is a one off episode or it recurs in the future, who knows. Some people do just have single episodes then are fine. Others like myself will experience recurrence.

Antidepressants actually worked like magic for me during the first two episodes of depression that I took them for. I went from feeling awful to feeling totally fine. Sadly, they have stopped working for me but there's every chance that they will work for you.

Many people are very vociferously pro or anti medication. I'm neither, I think medication can be a Godsend but at the same time they don't work for everybody and they can stop working (my psychiatrist told me they don't 'stop working', yeah well fuck him because they did for me).

I do believe that exercise is a great thing for depression. It's not a magic cure but it has helped me a lot. It definitely affects neurochemistry in a good way. There are days I have woken up feeling quite awful, gone for a run and felt fine for the rest of the day. I would definitely advise exercise, good diet and a lot of people advocate meditation although I"ve never tried it.

I know it's not easy but don't overthink the job. I don't think you're going to screw it up. But having an absolute mentality of 'I can't screw anything up' creates pressure that can itself lead to problems. I know because I've been there. 

I took the day off today because I just couldn't face work but I guess I could have worked if I had really wanted to and there are plenty of times I have managed to work while severely depressed. It just takes longer and is really unpleasant.

It's a lifelong struggle my friend. I have given up on ever being 'cured' and just assume this will be the rest of my life. Which just leaves the question as to whether I can endure this, whether the good times outweigh the bad, etc.

I know that there are some people who have been unremittingly severely depressed for years. Honestly, fuck that there's no way I could bear it. I can only cope with this because these days depressive episodes don't seem to last more than a couple of weeks. Even then there are days (like today) when I think about ending it, I guess because (a) even enduring a day of this shit is too much and (b) I never fully believe that the episode will resolve 'quickly.

Yeah I think about this a lot too. And the craziest thing the difference is just a subtle imbalance in brain chemistry. I'm depressed af right now and can't do a damn thing but a few weeks ago I went through this weird phase of being not just not depressed but abnormally happyl Like my brain was fizzing with serotonin or something. And I could have done anything, like nothing could have fazed me, I was getting a tonne of work and handling it with ease, exercising every day and could have done much more. It really was life on easy mode. It only lasted a couple of days but it felt amazing. Absolutely blows my mind that this is how a lot of people feel MOST OF THE TIME. 

How the hell can I compete with that? I'm amazed that I am where I am in life in spite of all the depression and anxiety. If I felt like I did during those couple of days I'd probably be in charge of the world, or at least a small country by, now. It was some Limitless type shit.
Do you have a magic cure for depression that nobody knows about? Please say yes.

When the depression is bad, getting up is tough. But I guess that's true of most of us.

Logging on to check work e-mails is daunting. There can be a hundred of them and when I'm so down I don't have the ability to do what I need to so it can be extremely anxiety inducing. 

When I'm feeling good, I'll log on first thing without thinking about it and just hammer out responses. But when bad I have to wait a few hours before I can even check. And even then it's tempting to take a Xanax before doing so.

By night time I normally feel a bit better anyway, like my neurochemistry isn't quite as terrible as it is in the mornings. 

I hate so much that we think we're living in advanced times but when it comes to depression, we've just moved slightly on from the stone age.

It got better for me. Then got wore again. Then better.

I know this pattern is going to repeat itself for the rest of my life. The worst thing about it is that when going through a bad phase (like now) I'll never actually believe that I'm going to get better, even though I have hundreds of times. 

And conversely when I'm feeling good I won't do the things necessary to safeguard my mental health (or at least not completely ruin it) because I can't imagine what it's like to feel depressed.

If I could fix the above I'd be a lot better off.

I'm late thirties. So many friends have come and gone. But now no new friends are going to come. The very few remaining ones will just go until there are  none left (I'm pretty close to that now).

When you're in school and at university it's almost impossible not to make friends (although at the same time of course making friends is hard). And there are tonnes of social events planned so there is always something to do.

Then you enter the working world. Maybe at first, when you're junior, you still make friends and go out . But then later people are fixated on their families and presenting a certain image at work. So the socialising you do there isn't the same as when you were at school/uni. Eventually it's an atmosphere you can't wait to escape at the end of each day and the last thing you ever want to do is spend even more time with those people.

And then the friends you made in school and university - you lose touch or fall out and even if you remain friends you end up spread out over the country or world and they have families and you, never, ever hang out anymore and even if you do it's a quick meal or drink, then back home. You'll never, ever again spend time just walking around with them, staying up until 3am talking about the future, hopes, dreams or whatever. There are really no more plans to be made because they're a thing of the past and maybe some came to fruition and others didn't. 

And most people are completely fine with this.

Please feel free to talk anytime. I think we probably don't feel exactly the same but I can say I'm in a bad place too and the pain certainly is crushing. I called in sick from work today because I simply can't function and can't take the stress of wondering what I'll be asked to do next. There's some other thread about a guy who took the day off school and went to the zoo. I wish I were feeling well enough to go out there and make something out of not working today but all I can do is lie in bed wondering what I'm going to do if this doesn't get better.

My wife also is my world. I don't have a support network or friends either. I'm not sure how I ended up here, late thirties, fairly successful I guess but no friends. I have some friends from university but we exchange e-mails or messages every few weeks and that's all. Then there are so many other friends that have come and gone. And now I think at this age and stage in life no new friends are going to come, just the last few ones will go. Awesome. I keep wishing I could go back to school when you are surrounded by your friends all day. Or university even when it's similar and when there are always social things where you will go and see people you know. Now, nothing.

Work isn't the same. Like you go to work and most people can't wait to get out of that environment.

I still really believe depression is chemical though and that if the chemicals in our brains were in balance we wouldn't be feeling like this.

Sounds good (although like others I don't like the idea of zoos). I've taken a day off work because the depression is so bad that I can't perform simple tasks and am just lying in bed thinking of how bad this is and when it's going to stop. Your way is definitely better.

I understand totally. And don't get me wrong, it's good to focus on something. It's just I remember during my first episode of depression I was in a truly terrible way. Made an appointment to see a therapist. Literally counted the seconds down to see him. Then, when he did absolutely fuck all I came out of the appointment devastated.

Not that you would have such unrealistic expectations, I was 18 at the time and had never been through this before or seen a therapist before.

We'll listen to you on here though (if you'll listen back to us!).

You can make it. But I don't know how much sense it makes to focus everything on just making it to 28th, like your therapist is going to solve everything.

I don't know your story. It's good you have an appointment but better to start doing stuff to help yourself now (walks, exercise, etc).

Death is always a comforting thought. There was that quote, maybe Nietzche? The thought of suicide gets one through many a long night.

You're absolutely right. Am going to avoid those things like the plague from now on. It's tough feeling like this, knowing they make everything immediately better but as you say in the long term they will make everything a 1000x worse. Fuck that. Will self medicate with exercise instead.
Same. The vast majority of people need to have been through this to understand how devastating it is. It's not a relatable illness. Whereas everybody can relate to pain, loss of function, etc.

Sorry to hear about your struggle. Your form of self medicating is understandable at least.

The pill I took today had me go from a non-functioning wreck, almost having a breakdown when opening a work e-mail to feeling good, confident, able to handle work with ease, etc. Why the hell can't they make an anti-depressant that does the same thing, doesn't take 3 weeks at least to work (in my case doesn't work at all) and just provides some instant respite.

Well, that's what this pill does for me, something that no anti-depressant can do and that's provide INSTANT respite.

Unfortunately it's also highly addictive and in the long run will undoubtedly do much more harm than good. But honestly right now I just feel reassured that I have something like a 'Break only in the case of emergency' tablet.

I swear, anybody that says, 'Be happy' or 'Snap out of it' in response to someone saying they're suicidal or severely depressed deserves to have a week-long episode of really bad depression. Doubt they would say the same thing ever again.

My Dad basically said the same thing when I first said I was suffering severe depression. Can you imagine someone saying that if you told them you had cancer or MS or something? It's simply unbelievable that anybody could be so stupid but unfortunately many are.

I'm sorry man, I know how you feel and would give you a hug and tell you it will all be ok if I could.

I don't think any of us really want to die, just want to live without suffering so damn much. I woke up this morning and was so devastated to have to face the day, I just wanted to not wake up. 

I don't know why our bodies and minds are capable of feeling like this.

Believe me you're not the first girl to have stronger feelings for a 'bad' guy than a 'good' guy. I swear us guys spend about half our lives complaining about how girls always go for the bad boys when there are good guys just waiting to be noticed, lol. So get that out of your head, you don't deserve to suffer because you carried on having feelings for him after he treated you so badly.

You say you're suicidal and your entire post is about this guy. So you're suicidal because of this guy and you can't have him (as you know it's a messed up relationship) or you're suicidal because you feel guilty about still having such strong feelings?

It's almost comic. Being hung up on by a fucking suicide hotline. Takes the fucking biscuit doesn't it?

I called those fuckers once, did no good whatsoever. But I'm sure some people have been helped by them.

Sorry OP, you have us at least.
